selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the first spiritual benefit mentioned for someone who works in a garden with a proper intention?
questions.answer: That person receives a share in the worshipful praise made by the plants and trees he cultivates.

questions.question: According to the passage, what condition is attached to gaining that first benefit?
questions.answer: The work must be done with a sound and sincere intention.

questions.question: What is the second benefit connected to the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Whatever is consumed from it can count like charity on the worker’s behalf.

questions.question: Who can eat from the produce and still make that second benefit apply?
questions.answer: Any creature or person mentioned there, including animals, people, customers, and even thieves.

questions.question: What two attitudes must a person have for the produce to count like charity?
questions.answer: He must work for Allah’s sake and stay within what Allah allows, while seeing himself as a caretaker distributing Allah’s property.

questions.question: Why does leaving the required prayers lead to a major loss in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the person misses both spiritual gains, loses motivation, and is deprived of a deeper meaning in his work.

questions.question: How is the prayerless person described over time as he gets older?
questions.answer: He becomes tired of his work, loses heart, and drifts into laziness.

questions.question: What kind of thinking pushes that person toward idleness?
questions.answer: He thinks he will soon leave the world anyway, so he sees no reason to keep struggling.

questions.question: How does the other person think differently about work and worship?
questions.answer: He sees both lawful work and worship as ways to prepare for the grave and the next life, so he works with more energy.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage draw between the two workers?
questions.answer: One becomes spiritually bankrupt and discouraged, while the other becomes more purposeful, hopeful, and hardworking.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the image of the “first mine” represent?
questions.answer: It represents a hidden spiritual gain a person receives through sincere work in the garden.

questions.question: How does the passage connect farming or gardening with worship?
questions.answer: It teaches that ordinary work can bring spiritual reward when it is done with the right intention and in obedience to Allah.

questions.question: What does the “second mine” add beyond the first one?
questions.answer: It adds the reward of ongoing charity when others benefit from what the garden produces.

questions.question: Does the second reward depend only on the produce itself, or also on the worker’s outlook and method?
questions.answer: It also depends on the worker’s outlook and method, especially acting within Allah’s permission and for His sake.

questions.question: Why is the worker told to see himself as a distributor rather than an owner in an absolute sense?
questions.answer: Because the passage teaches that the true ownership belongs to Allah, and the worker is only delivering what Allah provides.

questions.question: What happens to the person who abandons the prescribed prayers, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He loses these two great gains and ends up with weakened spirit and poor motivation.

questions.question: In what sense does the passage call that person “bankrupt”?
questions.answer: He is spiritually emptied of the rewards and meanings that could have enriched his life and work.

questions.question: What emotional change happens in the neglectful person as old age comes?
questions.answer: His interest fades, and he becomes worn out and detached from his work.

questions.question: What future-oriented goal gives the first man strength?
questions.answer: He wants to prepare light for the grave and provision for the life to come.

questions.question: What major lesson about prayer and daily work comes out of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Prayer does not take away from meaningful work; instead, it gives work spiritual value, purpose, and lasting reward.

questions.question: What practical setting is used in the passage to explain the lesson?
questions.answer: The lesson is explained through the example of working in a garden.

questions.question: What is gained from flowers and fruit-bearing trees when the intention is right?
questions.answer: A share in the glorification and praise connected with those living things.

questions.question: Why is intention so central in the first part of the passage?
questions.answer: Because the outward action alone is not enough; the inner purpose turns the work into something spiritually rewarding.

questions.question: What kinds of eaters are included in the discussion of the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Both expected and unexpected users are included, from people and animals to even those who take it wrongly.
